claims.text: 5th Avenue & Pine Street had 167 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 2 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $11.4 million a year.
12% of crashes here were recorded as “pedestrian” crashes, against 8% at the city's worst crash locations.
5% of crashes here were recorded as “motor vehicle struck motorized scooter, front end at angle” crashes, against 2% at the city's worst crash locations.
5% of crashes here were recorded as “from same direction - one left turn - one straight” crashes, against 1% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 5.0 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $1.7 million a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Lighting would avoid about 3.6 crashes a year (CMF 7774, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $1.2 million a year; check on site: the corner has no street lighting now.
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 4th Avenue, 5th Avenue, Pine Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
